result_summary: GTM plan for task 167, grounded in two tool reads. Pricing catalog is fresh (catalog_as_of 2026-10-14, staleness_days 4, stale=false, 50/50 rows), so its comparisons can be quoted as a dated research snapshot, not live pricing. Macro snapshot is unavailable — inflation, CPI and FX are all null because no fresh snapshot exists in this process — so all figures below are nominal USD and no real-terms or currency adjustment is possible; re-check before any annual commitment. ICP (to lock this week): North American SMBs, 2-50 employees, owner or one marketing/generalist operator, $500K-$10M revenue, already paying for a point solution or a human/agency for marketing, sales or support and currently spending $500-$3,000/mo on it. The catalog shows that band explicitly: social media management for a small business $500-$2,000/mo, SEO for a small business $1,500-$3,000/mo over 15-25 hours, AI automation agency retainers $500-$8,000/mo, productized subscriptions $199/mo (bookkeeping) to $699-$2,599/mo (unlimited design). Positioning: the 10+ hours/week promise is priced at roughly 2-10% of the equivalent human cost — a real wedge, but with every KPI at zero (0 customers, $0 MRR, 0% CAC, $0 LTV, 0% churn, 0 NPS) it is an untested claim, so the plan leads with one job (automate inbound lead follow-up and first-response support) rather than three promises at once. Pricing validation: $49 Starter is below every comparable human-delivered service and mid-tier productized subscription in the catalog, and sits in the same price band as the cheapest AI-native point tools (Pilot $99, unverified Synthetic claim $49, Rosie $49) — so it reads as a point tool, not a replacement for a $1,500/mo SEO retainer, which undercuts the 10-hours value story. $149 Pro is still only 7-30% of the cheapest comparable human retainer. Recommendation: keep $49/$149 as published for the first cohort but add a $399/mo 'Done-with-you' tier anchored against the $500-$2,000 social retainer floor, and test it in the first ten sales conversations. Path to Q1 2026 goals in unit-economics terms, all unmeasured inputs labelled assumptions to test: at a blended $80/mo ARPA (assumption: 70% Starter / 30% Pro), $10K MRR needs ~125 paying accounts, which is above the 100-customer goal — so the goal only closes if blended ARPA reaches ~$100/mo (about 60% Pro mix or 20% of accounts on a $399 tier). $10K MRR and 100 paying customers are therefore not simultaneously reachable at today's published mix; that conflict must be resolved by tier mix, not by discounting. CAC, LTV, churn and conversion are all unmeasured (the ad platforms have no credentials and no metrics were read this cycle, Stripe revenue is unverified), so no payback or funnel-yield number is asserted here; the plan's first deliverable is instrumentation — trial start, activation, conversion to paid, ARPA and voluntary churn — so the next planning run can replace assumptions with measurements. v2 scope must contain only what the ICP's single lead job requires: (1) CRM/mailbox/helpdesk connectors, (2) the inbound lead follow-up and first-response automation playbook with editable guardrails, (3) a hours-saved dashboard that produces the first real proof point for the value proposition, (4) self-serve checkout and metering so revenue is measurable, and (5) reporting/export that lets us prove the promise per account.
